title: Strata — memory is explicit I/O
excerpt: Strata is a prototype 64-bit instruction set where memory is explicit I/O, caches are software, capabilities name everything, and there are no interrupts. With a Verilog implementation and an emulator that run in the browser, the StrataOS microkernel, and four languages: Forth, Stratalk (a Smalltalk), Stralog (a Prolog) and a self-hosting C compiler.
content_html:
01The idea

Modern CPUs pretend memory is flat and fast, then spend a third of the chip keeping up the pretence. Strata stops pretending. What software can reach directly is small and fast; everything else is a transfer you ask for, and can overlap with work.

Local Stores, not caches

Loads and stores reach only registers and a 64 KiB data Local Store per core. Instructions come only from a 64 KiB instruction Local Store. L1 is an architectural scratchpad, and software decides what lives there.

Transfers, as if synchronous

tget, tput and tgetx move data between tiers with completion tags. Each takes effect at its issue point; the hardware stalls any access to a range still in flight. Overlap is a performance choice, never a correctness one.

Linear capabilities

Far memory is named only through capabilities. Writable ones can be split, joined, given to another core and taken back — never copied. A data race is not something you can write down. Revocation domains take everything back at once.

No interrupts

A device “interrupts” by completing a transfer. tany waits for any of a set of transfers, or for a capability arriving in the inbox. Ctrl-C is a console read that completes when you press the key. The timer is a read that completes at a deadline.

02The tiers, all visible

Registersx0–x31 · c0–c15

Local Stores64 KiB I-LS + 64 KiB D-LS per core · load/store

T2 cluster store256 KiB · tget / tput

T3 system memory64 MiB · tget / tput / tamo

Devicesconsole · disk · timer · framebuffer

; divide the work by dividing ownership
        csplit c5, c0, s6     ; c0 = my piece, c5 = the rest
        csplit c8, c5, s6     ; c5 = core k's piece
        cgive  c5, s3         ; hand it over (c5 is now empty)
        ...
        ctake  c5, s3         ; take it back from core k only
        cjoin  c0, c5         ; and glue the array together

; stream far data while computing
        tget   tg1, a0, c0, t0, t1   ; ask for the next block
        ...                          ; work on the current one
        twait  tg1                   ; (loads would wait anyway)

03StrataOS

A microkernel written in Strata assembly, where the explicit machine shows through instead of being hidden. Its architecture, the kernel, and every server's messages →

A kernel that pages itself

A few kilobytes stay resident. The rest of the kernel is code units it loads into its own instruction store on demand — the same xcall / xmiss mechanism programs use.

Servers are processes

proc, dev, fs, tty, pipe and the window server ws run in user mode. A message is a lent buffer capability; programs talk to servers directly, core to core, in hardware.

Context switches you can see

Preemptive multitasking with a configurable time slice (2 ms by default, down to 100 µs). A switch copies the used Local Store out and in — the cache flush other CPUs hide. ps shows each process's switches and kilobytes moved; the window server's core lattice pulses with every one.

strata$ seq 30 | grep 2 | wc      # three processes, two pipes
strata$ -n 3 mandel &             # three threads, time-shared
strata$ as < hello.s > hi && hi   # the assembler, written in Strata
strata$ ps                        # switches and KiB moved, per process
strata$ ws                        # the window server takes the screen

The window server

ws is the only process that touches the framebuffer. It tiles windows on a grid, and makes the machine visible: the strip at the top has one cell per core, lit in the colour of the process running there, pulsing on every context switch; each window's tag shows how many kilobytes its context switches have moved. Clients draw in their own memory and lend each finished band to the server as a capability; only the server writes the screen.

04Strata Forth

A Forth bootstrapped the classic way — a small kernel of primitives in assembly, the rest of the language defined in Forth — with a modern twist: words compile to native Strata code. Because stores cannot write instruction memory, every definition is assembled in data memory, written to far memory and installed with tgetx: a JIT whose install step you can watch.

  • Inlining, constant folding and tail calls
  • Capabilities, transfers and tags as ordinary words
  • far@ / far! through a software cache built on ltag / linst
  • spawn / await across cores
  • Locals, quotations, catch/throw, see

Every word, with its source, and a playground →
Try Forth in your browser →

: sq ( n -- n*n ) dup * ;  ok
7 sq . 49  ok
see sq
: sq  ( xt $8100 , 40 bytes)
  8100:  addi sp, sp, -8
  8104:  sd   ra, 0(sp)
  8108:  addi s0, s0, -8
  810c:  sd   s1, 0(s0)
  8110:  ld   t0, 0(s0)
  8114:  addi s0, s0, 8
  8118:  mul  s1, t0, s1
  811c:  ld   ra, 0(sp)
  8120:  addi sp, sp, 8
  8124:  ret
 ok
: sum-sq ( n -- ) 0 swap 0 do i sq + loop ;  ok
100 sum-sq . 328350  ok

05Stratalk, a Smalltalk

A Smalltalk whose object memory follows the machine. New objects are made near, in a nursery in the core's data store; the survivors are written out to far memory in one transfer. Far objects are read through a software cache on ltag / linst, and every far store is a transfer you can count. Frames page out to a far stack when recursion runs deep, and a JIT written in Stratalk compiles hot methods into code units that StrataOS pages into the instruction store.

  • Pharo's syntax, closures with non-local return, ANSI exceptions, large integers
  • A compiler written in Stratalk, checked byte for byte against the bootstrap one
  • A REPL with completion; files; a workspace, class browser and inspector in the window server
  • Every StrataOS server's messages as classes, generated from their specifications

The classes, the examples and a playground →

strata$ stratalk
st> 100 factorial printString size
158
st> [10 / 0] on: ZeroDivide do: [:e | e messageText]
'division by zero'
st> (1 to: 10) inject: 0 into: [:a :b | a + b]
55
st> Smalltalk vm at: 'scavenges'
32

06Stralog, a Prolog

A Prolog in Strata assembly whose terms all live in far memory, reached only by transfers. The data Local Store holds windows onto the tops of the heap, the trail and the choicepoint stack, and a small write-back cache for everything else; the engine slides a window or spills it with an explicit tget or tput, and statistics counts every byte that moved.

  • ISO core Prolog: cut, if-then-else, call/N, catch/throw with ISO error terms
  • Assert and retract, findall, bagof/setof, DCGs, op/3
  • 584 of 596 ISO conformance vectors pass
  • An engine bigger than the instruction store, in code units StrataOS pages in

Every predicate, the examples and a playground →
Try Stralog in your browser →

strata$ -m 8 stralog
?- append(X, Y, [1, 2]).
X = [], Y = [1,2] ;
X = [1], Y = [2] ;
X = [1,2], Y = [] ;
false.
?- [queens].
true.
?- count_queens(8, N).
N = 92.
?- [family].
true.
?- findall(D, ancestor(tom, D), Ds).
Ds = [bob,liz,ann,pat,jim].
?- statistics.
calls: 134488
heap: 4112 of 6899712 bytes used; window: 485 spills, 1857 slides, 2090432 bytes moved
garbage collections: 0, 0 bytes given back
trail: 16 bytes used; window: 1 spills, 1 slides, 512 bytes moved
choicepoints: 4 frames; window: 0 spills, 0 slides, 0 bytes moved
far cache: 74618 misses, 5583 write-backs (64-byte lines)
atoms: 16616 bytes, clauses: 90352 bytes, findall: 0 bytes
true.

07C, compiled on the machine

cc is a C99 compiler that runs inside StrataOS and writes program images directly: one pass, no assembler, no linker. It is written in C and compiles itself; the first compiler, cc0, is the same language in Strata assembly, and compiling the compiler with itself twice gives the same bytes as the cc on the disk.

  • Both compilers pass 521 tests from the suites of two other C compilers
  • asm("...") and intrinsics for what only Strata has: transfers, capabilities
  • 106 KiB of compiler in a 32 KiB instruction store: it pages itself
  • The same source builds as a cross compiler on your machine

The bootstrap, the machine from C, the tests →
Compile C on Strata in your browser →

strata$ cc /src/hi.c
strata$ hi there
Hello from C on Strata, there!
strata$ cc0 -p -h 0 -o cc1 /src/cc.c   # assembly compiles the compiler
strata$ cc1 -p -h 0 -o c2 /src/cc.c    # which compiles itself
strata$ cmp c2 /bin/cc
c2 /bin/cc: same

08Try it in your browser

The reference emulator, compiled to WebAssembly. Boot StrataOS on 12 cores and type at its shell, watch eight cores draw a Mandelbrot set into the framebuffer, or play the games. Each language has its own start: Forth, whose words run as native Strata code; Stratalk's REPL; Stralog's top level; C, compiled by the compiler on the disk. No install.

Run Strata in your browser

09Run it

Needs a C compiler and Verilator 5; SDL2 is optional (for the window). Or read it first: the source browser has every assembly, Forth and C program, syntax-coloured.

makeassembler, emulator and the Verilated RTL

make testevery example and an OS boot on both machines, compared instruction by instruction

make show-gfxopen the framebuffer window and watch eight cores draw

make bootboot StrataOS on the emulator

make fortha Forth prompt on bare metal

blocks.html_en: 05Stratalk, a Smalltalk

sentences.en: 05Stratalk, a Smalltalk

blocks.html_en: A Smalltalk whose object memory follows the machine. New objects are made near, in a nursery in the core's data store; the survivors are written out to far memory in one transfer. Far objects are read through a software cache on ltag / linst, and every far store is a transfer you can count. Frames page out to a far stack when recursion runs deep, and a JIT written in Stratalk compiles hot methods into code units that StrataOS pages into the instruction store.

blocks.html_en: 06Stralog, a Prolog

sentences.en: 06Stralog, a Prolog

blocks.html_en: A Prolog in Strata assembly whose terms all live in far memory, reached only by transfers. The data Local Store holds windows onto the tops of the heap, the trail and the choicepoint stack, and a small write-back cache for everything else; the engine slides a window or spills it with an explicit tget or tput, and statistics counts every byte that moved.

blocks.html_en: 07C, compiled on the machine

sentences.en: 07C, compiled on the machine

blocks.html_en: cc is a C99 compiler that runs inside StrataOS and writes program images directly: one pass, no assembler, no linker. It is written in C and compiles itself; the first compiler, cc0, is the same language in Strata assembly, and compiling the compiler with itself twice gives the same bytes as the cc on the disk.

blocks.html_en: 08Try it in your browser

sentences.en: 08Try it in your browser

blocks.html_en: The reference emulator, compiled to WebAssembly. Boot StrataOS on 12 cores and type at its shell, watch eight cores draw a Mandelbrot set into the framebuffer, or play the games. Each language has its own start: Forth, whose words run as native Strata code; Stratalk's REPL; Stralog's top level; C, compiled by the compiler on the disk. No install.
